title: Componentwise execution of the product protocol
statement:
Let $k$ be a natural number and, for each $i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,k$, let $p_i$ be a private-coin finite-message protocol with private-randomness types $\Omega_{X,i}$ for Alice and $\Omega_{Y,i}$ for Bob, common public input types $X$ and $Y$, and output type $\alpha_i$. Fix public inputs $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$, together with coin vectors $\omega_x \in \prod_{i} \Omega_{X,i}$ and $\omega_y \in \prod_{i} \Omega_{Y,i}$. Then executing the product protocol on these data agrees componentwise with executing each factor on its own coordinate of the randomness:
\[
  (\pi\,p).\mathrm{rrun}\;x\;y\;\omega_x\;\omega_y
  \;=\; \bigl(\, i \mapsto (p_i).\mathrm{rrun}\;x\;y\;(\omega_x\,i)\;(\omega_y\,i) \,\bigr).
\]
hypotheses_covered: a natural number $k$ indexing the family
a family of private-coin finite-message protocols $p_i$ over $\mathrm{Fin}\,k$ with heterogeneous randomness and output types but common inputs $X$, $Y$
Alice's coin vector $\omega_x$ in the product $\prod_i \Omega_{X,i}$
Bob's coin vector $\omega_y$ in the product $\prod_i \Omega_{Y,i}$
